prompt:
Q: Given an undirected graph with n vertices, no matter how you complete DFS, I can always complete
BFS in the same order. What can you say about this graph?
judge_reasoning: Candidate 2 correctly identifies that the graph must be complete, which matches the idea that BFS can only realize an arbitrary vertex order when all vertices are at distance 1 from the start. Candidates 1, 3, and 4 claim the graph is a path or a tree, but they don’t account for the BFS layering constraint versus adversarial DFS completions; DFS can force discoveries that BFS cannot reproduce. Their justifications are also too general (“trees minimize ambiguity”, “cycles introduce ambiguity”) without addressing the core ordering impossibility.
